newsitem.title: MEXICO: IMF's Fischer meets with Mexico's Zedillo, Ortiz.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Fischer meets with Mexico's Zedillo, Ortiz.

text.p: A top International Monetary Fund official met on Thursday with President Ernesto Zedillo and Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz and they discussed the Mexican economy.

"There was a brief examination of recent events in the Mexican economy and I think we share the same diagnosis," Ortiz told reporters after meeting with IMF First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer. He said the meeting was part social because Zedillo, a former central bank official, once studied under Fischer in the United States. Ortiz gave no more details.

Mexico has been negotiating a medium-term Extended Fund Facility with the IMF, following the expiry in February of its emergency $17.5 billion contingency credit program issued after the 1994 peso crash.

Mexican officials, pointing to a fast-recovering economy, say they are in no hurry to clinch the deal. But in June the government unveiled a three-year economic program that was praised by Fischer and could form the basis for an agreement with the IMF.
The IMF is believed to be keen to clinch a deal to keep close tabs on Mexico's economic progress. The country is still one of the IMF's biggest borrowers, with some $10 billion outstanding.
Mexican government officials gave no details on the expected length or motive of Fischer's visit.
